biodiversity_overview.text: 860 GBIF occurrence records for 21 tracked species are attributed to Sikkim, spanning 1873-2026.
838 of these records (97.4%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 10, Magnoliopsida 6, Mammalia 3, Squamata 1, Pinopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 3 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian White-eye (296), Indian Cuckoo (293), Indian Blue Robin (137), Mango (38), Indian Gooseberry (33).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 69 in 2016 to 242 in 2024. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 30.33% of Sikkim's area (10 areas intersect the state).
9.3% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (78 of 838); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Spikenard (0.64), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Acacia-tree (0.26), Mountain Chiffchaff (0.20), Mango (0.18).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Sikkim (equal-weight reference): cell near 28.125N 88.875E (overall rank 377, median rank across weightings 364); cell near 27.375N 88.875E (overall rank 424, median rank across weightings 413); cell near 27.375N 88.125E (overall rank 445, median rank across weightings 428).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 2,678 km2 (32.95% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

23.3 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.87% of the 2000 extent; 0.48% in 2015-2024, rank 19 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2023 (3.19 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.24% of land and population density is 82.9 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
27% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
